roadmap.title: Neural Networks Learning Roadmap (Academic Focus)
roadmap.description: A structured roadmap for learning neural networks with an academic focus, suitable for individuals with intermediate math and coding proficiency and a medium time investment.
roadmap.target_audience: Students, researchers, and professionals seeking a theoretical and practical understanding of neural networks.

assumptions.math_proficiency: Intermediate: Familiar with linear algebra (vectors, matrices, operations), calculus (derivatives, gradients), and probability/statistics.
assumptions.coding_proficiency: Intermediate: Comfortable with Python and basic data structures, able to write and debug functions and classes.
assumptions.learning_purpose: Academic: Emphasis on understanding the underlying principles and mathematical foundations of neural networks.
assumptions.time_investment: Medium: Approximately 10-15 hours per week dedicated to learning.

stages.description: Review and solidify essential mathematical and programming concepts.

resources.title: Linear Algebra Review
resources.description: Focus on matrix operations, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and vector spaces. Khan Academy or 3Blue1Brown's Linear Algebra series are excellent resources.

resources.title: Calculus Review
resources.description: Review derivatives, gradients, chain rule, and optimization. Khan Academy's Calculus series is a good option.

resources.title: Python and NumPy Fundamentals
resources.description: Practice using NumPy for numerical computation, array manipulation, and linear algebra operations. Codecademy's Python courses are helpful.

key_milestones: Comfortable with matrix multiplication and vector operations.
Understand the concept of derivatives and gradients.
Proficient in using NumPy for array manipulation.
practical_projects: Implement basic matrix operations in NumPy.
Calculate the gradient of a simple function using NumPy.

stages.description: Learn the basic building blocks of neural networks, including perceptrons, activation functions, and the feedforward process.

resources.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning by Michael Nielsen (Online)
resources.description: Excellent introductory text covering basic concepts and implementation.

resources.title: Deep Learning Specialization on Coursera by Andrew Ng
resources.description: Provides a comprehensive introduction to neural networks and deep learning.

resources.title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks (Glorot & Bengio, 2010)
resources.description: Introduce challenges in neural network training, such as vanishing gradient problems, and discuss techniques like Xavier initialization.

key_milestones: Understand the architecture of a simple neural network.
Explain the role of activation functions.
Implement a forward pass through a neural network.
practical_projects: Implement a single-layer perceptron to classify data.
Experiment with different activation functions and observe their effects.
Build a simple feedforward neural network using NumPy.

stages.description: Understand the backpropagation algorithm and different optimization techniques used to train neural networks.

resources.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning by Michael Nielsen (Online)
resources.description: Chapters on backpropagation and gradient descent.

resources.title: Deep Learning by Goodfellow, Bengio, and Courville
resources.description: Detailed explanation of backpropagation and optimization algorithms.

resources.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization (Kingma & Ba, 2014)

key_milestones: Derive the backpropagation algorithm for a simple neural network.
Implement backpropagation using NumPy.
Understand the concepts of gradient descent, momentum, and Adam optimization.
practical_projects: Implement backpropagation to train a neural network on a simple dataset (e.g., XOR).
Experiment with different optimization algorithms and learning rates.
Visualize the loss function and gradient descent process.

resources.description: Comprehensive tutorial covering the basics of PyTorch.

resources.title: TensorFlow Tutorial on TensorFlow Official Website
resources.description: Comprehensive tutorial covering the basics of TensorFlow.

resources.description: Learn how to use Keras (a high-level API) for building deep learning models.

key_milestones: Understand the basic concepts of tensors and computational graphs.
Build and train a simple neural network using PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Utilize datasets and data loaders provided by the framework.
practical_projects: Re-implement previous projects using PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Train a neural network on the MNIST dataset for handwritten digit recognition.
Experiment with different network architectures and hyperparameters.

stages.description: Explore advanced topics in neural networks, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and autoencoders.

resources.title: Deep Learning by Goodfellow, Bengio, and Courville
resources.description: Chapters on convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and autoencoders.

resources.title: Convolutional Neural Networks Specialization on Coursera by Andrew Ng
resources.description: In-depth coverage of CNNs and their applications.

resources.title: Sequence Models Specialization on Coursera by Andrew Ng
resources.description: In-depth coverage of RNNs and their applications.

resources.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Hinton, 2012)
resources.description: Learn about one of the groundbreaking CNN architectures.

key_milestones: Understand the architecture and functionality of CNNs and RNNs.

Implement an RNN for sequence modeling.
Understand the concept of autoencoders and their applications.
practical_projects: Train a CNN on the CIFAR-10 dataset.
Build a simple character-level RNN for text generation.
Implement an autoencoder for dimensionality reduction or anomaly detection.

roadmap.conclusion: This roadmap provides a structured path for learning neural networks with an academic focus. Remember to stay curious, experiment, and consult multiple resources to deepen your understanding.  Continuously explore new research papers and emerging techniques to stay up-to-date in this rapidly evolving field.
notes: The estimated time for each stage is approximate and depends on the individual's learning pace and background.
The recommended resources are suggestions and can be substituted with other similar resources.
The practical projects are designed to reinforce the concepts learned in each stage. Modify and expand upon them to further your understanding.
Prioritize understanding the underlying mathematical principles of neural networks for academic success.

roadMap.title: Understanding Basic Concepts & Definitions
roadMap.description: Focus on grasping the fundamental definitions and concepts of Newton's Laws without delving into complex calculations. Relate these concepts to everyday experiences.

resources.name: Crash Course Physics #5 - Newton's Laws of Motion
resources.notes: A quick overview of Newton's three laws with relatable examples.

resources.name: Khan Academy - Newton's Laws of Motion
resources.notes: Focus on the introductory articles and videos explaining each law.

resources.name: Physics for Dummies - Chapter on Newton's Laws
resources.link: N/A (Search for 'Physics for Dummies Newton's Laws')
resources.notes: Offers a simplified explanation, if preferred over online resources.

keyMilestones: Define inertia, force, mass, and acceleration.
State Newton's three laws of motion in simple terms.
Provide real-world examples of each law.
practicalProjects: Observe everyday situations and identify how Newton's laws apply (e.g., pushing a shopping cart, a ball rolling down a hill).
Think about what would happen if one of Newton's laws suddenly stopped working.

roadMap.title: Newton's First Law (Inertia)
roadMap.description: Explore the concept of inertia in detail, focusing on how objects resist changes in their state of motion. Minimize math; prioritize conceptual understanding.

resources.name: MinutePhysics - Inertia
resources.notes: Concise explanation of inertia with visuals.

resources.name: PhET Simulation - Forces and Motion: Basics
resources.notes: Play with the simulation to observe inertia in action.  Just push the object and watch it go!

keyMilestones: Explain why objects at rest stay at rest, and objects in motion stay in motion (at a constant velocity).
Differentiate between mass and weight (conceptually, not mathematically).
Understand that inertia is proportional to mass.
practicalProjects: Place an object on a skateboard/roller skates and observe how it moves when you push/stop the skateboard.
Discuss why wearing a seatbelt is important in terms of inertia.

roadMap.title: Newton's Second Law (F=ma) - Conceptual Understanding
roadMap.description: Introduce the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration (F=ma) without complex calculations. Focus on the qualitative relationship: More force means more acceleration; more mass means less acceleration.

resources.name: Khan Academy - Newton's Second Law
resources.notes: Focus on the conceptual understanding of the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration.

resources.name: PhET Simulation - Forces and Motion: Basics
resources.notes: Experiment with changing the force and mass and observing the resulting acceleration. This simulation will clearly show the F=ma relation. Use 'Motion' tab.

keyMilestones: Explain that a force is required to change an object's velocity.
Describe how the magnitude of acceleration is directly proportional to the force applied.
Describe how the magnitude of acceleration is inversely proportional to the mass of the object.
practicalProjects: Compare pushing a light box versus a heavy box. Which one accelerates more easily? Why?
Observe the effect of different strength pushes on a toy car. How does the speed change?

roadMap.title: Newton's Third Law (Action-Reaction)
roadMap.description: Explore the concept of action-reaction pairs, focusing on identifying the forces acting between two interacting objects.

resources.name: Veritasium - Misconceptions About Newton's Third Law
resources.notes: Addresses common misconceptions about the third law.

resources.name: HyperPhysics - Newton's Third Law
resources.notes: A concise explanation of the third law with examples.

keyMilestones: State that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
Identify the action-reaction pair in different scenarios (e.g., pushing a wall, walking).
Understand that action and reaction forces act on *different* objects.
practicalProjects: Push against a wall and feel the wall pushing back on you.
Observe a rocket launch and identify the action (exhaust gases expelled) and reaction (rocket moving forward).
Bounce a ball. What are the action and reaction forces?

roadMap.title: Putting It All Together & Next Steps
roadMap.description: Review all three laws and consider how they interact.  If interested, brainstorm potential coding projects or deeper dives into physics. This is the optional exploration stage.

resources.name: The Science Classroom - Newton's Laws Summary
resources.notes: Find a short video summarizing all three laws.

keyMilestones: Explain how all three laws contribute to understanding motion.
Identify areas of personal interest for further exploration (e.g., projectile motion, friction).
Brainstorm potential coding projects (e.g., a simple simulation of a falling object).
practicalProjects: Consider how Newton's Laws apply to a sport you enjoy.
If interested in coding, sketch out the design for a simple simulation showing an object obeying Newton's Laws. Don't code yet, just plan.

Calculate force given mass and acceleration (F=ma).

roadmap.description: Follow along with a well-commented implementation of a simple neural network in Python using NumPy. Focus on understanding the code line by line rather than writing it from scratch.
resources: Michael Nielsen's 'Neural Networks and Deep Learning' (Chapter 1: Using neural nets to recognize handwritten digits): [http://neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com/chapter1.html] (Read the code walkthrough, don't try to implement from scratch yet)

YouTube: Sentdex's 'Neural Networks from Scratch' - Simple explanation on a basic NN (skip forward propagation and back propagation section) [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wo5dMEPIfNQ&list=PLQVvvaa0QuDcgIVK9MkxY4Y7t2s6L141L&index=3]
roadmap.milestone: Be able to trace the flow of data through a simple neural network implementation, understand the role of each line of code, and identify the key steps (forward pass, backpropagation).
roadmap.project: Modify the code from Michael Nielsen's book to change the number of neurons in a layer or the learning rate and observe the effect on the network's performance. Only make small incremental changes.

roadmap.title: Stage 4: Introduction to Deep Learning Frameworks (TensorFlow/Keras)
roadmap.description: Get a brief overview of deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow and Keras, focusing on their role in simplifying neural network development.  Understand the high-level abstractions they provide.
resources: TensorFlow's Quickstart for Beginners: [https://www.tensorflow.org/tutorials/quickstart/beginner]
Keras' Getting Started Guide: [https://keras.io/getting_started/]
YouTube: 'What is TensorFlow?' by Google Developers: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2eKjyr9vW3U]
roadmap.milestone: Understand the advantages of using deep learning frameworks and be able to build and train a simple neural network using Keras (e.g., a MNIST classifier) following a tutorial.
roadmap.project: Run the TensorFlow or Keras Quickstart tutorial and modify the network architecture (e.g., add or remove a layer) to see how it affects performance. Do not try to understand all the intricacies of TF or Keras.

roadmap.title: Stage 1: Newton's Laws - The Big Picture
roadmap.description: Gain a conceptual understanding of Newton's three laws of motion without getting bogged down in heavy math. Focus on real-world examples and visualizations.
resources: Khan Academy: Physics Library - Motion and Forces (Introductory videos)
MinutePhysics: Newton's Laws Explained (YouTube)
Hyperphysics: Newton's Laws (Conceptual explanations and diagrams)
roadmap.milestone: Ability to verbally explain each of Newton's laws and provide at least three real-world examples for each law.
roadmap.project: Observe everyday objects in motion (e.g., a rolling ball, a bouncing object, a person walking). Identify which of Newton's Laws are most prominent in each scenario and explain why.

roadmap.title: Stage 2: Force Diagrams and Basic Math
roadmap.description: Learn how to draw free-body diagrams to represent forces acting on objects. Introduce the basic formula F=ma and practice simple calculations involving force, mass, and acceleration. Cover vector basics: components and simple addition.
resources: Physics Classroom: Drawing Free-Body Diagrams
OpenStax College Physics: Chapter 4: Newton's Laws of Motion (Section 4.3 & 4.4)
Paul Hewitt's 'Conceptual Physics' (selected chapters on force and motion)
roadmap.milestone: Successfully draw free-body diagrams for simple scenarios (e.g., a block on a table, a falling object). Correctly calculate force, mass, or acceleration given the other two.
roadmap.project: Analyze the forces acting on a book sitting on a table. Draw a free-body diagram and calculate the normal force exerted by the table on the book, given the book's mass.

roadmap.title: Stage 3: Friction and Inclined Planes
roadmap.description: Introduce friction (static and kinetic) and its effect on motion. Learn how to solve problems involving inclined planes, including resolving forces into components along the plane.
resources: Khan Academy: Friction and Inclined Planes
Flipping Physics: Introduction to Inclined Planes (YouTube)
University Physics with Modern Physics (14th Edition) - Chapter 5 (relevant sections on friction and inclined planes)
roadmap.milestone: Solve problems involving friction and inclined planes, including calculating the force of friction and the acceleration of an object sliding down an inclined plane.
roadmap.project: Measure the angle at which a toy car starts to slide down an adjustable ramp. Use this angle to estimate the coefficient of static friction between the car's tires and the ramp's surface. Compare this with reported values for similar materials.

roadmap.title: Stage 4: Introduction to Coding with Physics - Visualizations
roadmap.description: Use a simple programming environment (e.g., Processing or p5.js) to create basic visualizations of Newton's laws. Start with simulating simple motion and gradually add complexity.
resources: Processing.org: Getting Started Tutorial
Daniel Shiffman's 'The Nature of Code' (Online book focusing on physics simulations in Processing)
p5.js website: Examples and Tutorials
roadmap.milestone: Create a simple program that simulates the motion of an object under constant acceleration due to gravity (e.g., a bouncing ball).
roadmap.project: Develop a simulation of a block sliding down an inclined plane, incorporating friction. Allow the user to adjust the angle of the incline and the coefficient of friction and observe the resulting motion. Visualize the forces with vectors.
